payload.title: Rate-limit incoming webhooks per tenant
payload.goal: POST /webhooks answers 429 with a Retry-After header when one tenant sends more webhooks than the configured limit in the configured window. Put the limiter in src/lib/limiter.ts, wire it into src/routes/webhooks.ts (and src/app.ts if it needs shared state), and read the limit and the window through loadConfig() in src/config.ts with defaults. Add tests in test/webhooks.test.ts or a new test file.
acceptance: A tenant over the limit gets 429 with a Retry-After header
The limit and the window come from config, not constants in a route
The suite stays green with new tests for the 429 path

payload.text:
Finished the task from the prior run's diff.

What was already there: `rateLimitMax` / `rateLimitWindowMs` in `src/config.ts` and `RateLimiter` in `src/lib/limiter.ts`.
What I did:
- Added a shared `RateLimiter` to `Deps` in `src/app.ts` (`createDeps`).
- Wired the check into `POST /webhooks` in `src/routes/webhooks.ts`: reads limit/window from `deps.config`, returns 429 `{ error: 'rate limit exceeded' }` with a `Retry-After` header in seconds when over the limit.
- Added `test/rate-limit.test.ts`: 429 path with `Retry-After`, other tenants unaffected, limit honored from config, no audit entry on rejection, plus `RateLimiter` unit tests (per-key counting, window reset) and config env/default tests.
- Updated exact-equality assertions in `test/config.test.ts` to include the new fields.
- Verified locally: `bun run test` 36/36 green, `bun run typecheck` clean (daemon re-runs the suite itself).

decision: shared RateLimiter lives in Deps so all webhook requests share one per-process limiter
decision: rate-limit check runs after tenant validation and before body parsing/storage, and rejected webhooks write no audit entry
decision: limiter is an in-memory per-tenant fixed window keyed by tenant id
decision: tests: test/config.test.ts changed because exact-equality assertions omitted the new rateLimitMax/rateLimitWindowMs fields added for this task

What I did not finish: nothing required by the acceptance criteria; no persistence or cross-process limiting (in-memory only).
What I did not look at: the review-voice-policy skill (not relevant, no policy file touched), and route files other than webhooks beyond confirming `Deps` usage.
